problem: Existing EQA frameworks are planner-centric: the memory module is only consumed by the answering module, so planner and stopping module rely on the current observation alone, causing redundant re-exploration or premature stopping, especially on multi-target, multi-region questions.
motivation: Questions such as comparing sofas in two rooms need information from several regions to be retained and shared across all modules. Long-term memory in dynamic environments is also easily corrupted by noisy updates and irrelevant retrievals, so it needs careful update and retrieval design.
key_idea: Make memory the core of EQA: store structured text memories in a vector library, update them with a viewpoint-contrastive rule, and feed entropy-adaptively retrieved, module-specific memory into the planner, stopping module and answering module.
insight: Memory helps most when it is retrieved selectively and injected into every module. In the strategy ablation (Qwen3VL-7B), adding update alone barely helps (33.18 to 33.41), retrieval gives the big jump (39.69), and the entropy-based dynamic k reaches 41.95. In the module ablation, memory in the stopping module and answering module gives most of the accuracy gain, while adding it to the planner mainly cuts steps (0.61 to 0.4). Fixed k is sensitive: k=4 is best and larger k causes redundancy and hallucination.
method: Memory storage: each observation is converted by a VLM into structured text (room, objects, description); a CLIP-ViT-L encoder embeds it, and entries <index, pose, rotation, text, feature> are stored in a Faiss vector library. Per-scene memory persists across tasks and initializes later tasks in the same scene.

Viewpoint-contrastive update: an update is triggered only if the agent is near a known pose (position < β_p and angle < β_r), the similarity 0.5*SSIM + 0.5*CLIP cosine is high, and the FOV is not mostly black. The new memory then replaces the old entry with the same index; otherwise the memory is added as a new entry.

Entropy-adaptive retrieval: the query is matched by an L2 distance threshold α_e(1+Entropy(query feature)) plus a cosine threshold α_s. Ambiguous queries get a wider matching range, and separate queries q_p, q_s and q_a serve the planner, stopping module and answering module.
Dynamic k: k = ceil(k_min + β·Entropy(f_q)), where f_q is the normalized concat of the initial-observation and question features, so complex queries and scenes retrieve more memories.

Memory-guided planner: frontier-based exploration where the top-p frontiers by utility λ1·G−λ2·C are projected into the image as visual prompts. A VLM scores them against retrieved memory and the current view, and the agent picks the highest-relevance direction.

Memory-based stopping and answering: the VLM gives a 5-level stopping confidence from the current observation and retrieved memory, stopping at level C or higher or at the step limit. A retrieval-augmented VLM then answers from the retrieved memory.

MT-HM3D benchmark: 5-10 Habitat images per scene, GPT-4o generates multi-target/multi-region questions, GPT-4-mini filters them, and manual verification follows. It has 1,587 QA pairs over 500 HM3D scenes in four types (comparison, relationship, counting, attribute).

setting.backbone: Frozen off-the-shelf VLMs (GPT-4o, Qwen2-VL-7B, Qwen3VL-7B, VideoMind-7B, InternVideo2.5-8B, Spatialbot-3B, SpatialVLM-7B) plus CLIP-ViT-L encoder and YOLOv11 detector
setting.model_size: 7B for the main open VLM (3B-8B range across variants); GPT-4o is proprietary
setting.training_data: none (training-free; no fine-tuning reported, pretrained VLMs used as is)
setting.observation: egocentric RGB-D with pose, converted to an occupancy/TSDF map
setting.action_space: frontier-based waypoints (navigation to selected frontier points)
setting.simulator: Habitat-Sim (Explore-EQA setup), plus a real Unitree Go2 demo
setting.privileged: none (persistent per-scene memory from earlier questions is used only in the two-round setting)

results: On MT-HM3D, MemoryEQA with GPT-4o reaches 43.11% success versus 33.21% for ExploreEQA with GPT-4o (+9.9%), with fewer normalized steps. It also gets 61.4% on HM-EQA (vs 47.4% for ExploreEQA with GPT-4o) and the best OpenEQA GPT score in the table (33.69 with InternVideo2.5-8B). Gains hold across Video, Spatial and Visual VLMs.
limitations: Fixed retrieval thresholds and the k formula need per-setting hyperparameters, and the authors note a dynamic memory window could be better

The new MT-HM3D benchmark is built with GPT-4o/GPT-4-mini and compared mainly against a single baseline (ExploreEQA), so it is small and not independently validated; inference is slow (about 40 hours on one L40 for MT-HM3D)
Update mechanism gives little benefit in static scenes; real-world evaluation is only two qualitative demos
